newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Dairy Brands sets sale of ice-cream unit.
newsitem.headline: NZ Dairy Brands sets sale of ice-cream unit.

text.p: Dairy Brands NZ said on Monday it had completed a restructuring of its Killinchy brand ice-cream unit and was reviewing its ongoing ownership of the business.
"The company does not believe it can add significant further value to Killinchy," it said, adding it would shortly seek expressions of interest into purchasing the activity.
The brand is a leading premium sector product distributed nationally through major supermarket chains.
Dairy Brands also advised it was in discussions regarding potential direct milk supply contracts to existing milk product users "in order to add value to its considerable milk volumes".
"The potential impact of a direct supply contract is to provide additional profit and the opportunity to realise capital," the company added, without giving further details.
Property developer Apple Fields Ltd holds a 43.8 percent stake in Dairy Brands which it is seeking to sell.
